links.comparator_used: Plans reoptimized on fully automatic contours (rigid registration, DIR, deep-learning, patient-specific segmentation) compared with plans on manual contours
links.outcome: Dosimetric effect on the daily reoptimized plan of using automatic versus manual OAR and target contours
links.effect: Automatic OAR contours: dosimetric influence small (<5% prescribed dose in most cases), best with DIR. Automatic target contour: effect larger (>5% prescribed dose in most cases), so manual verification remains necessary. Compared with non-adaptive therapy, dose differences from automatic target contours were small and target coverage improved, especially with DIR.
links.tradeoff: Manual contouring is too slow for online adaptation, so manual adjustment time must be prioritized (target over OARs) during time-critical sessions.
links.quote: The results show that manual adjustment of OARs is rarely necessary and that several autocontouring techniques are directly usable.
